background: QNB is the largest bank in the Middle East and Africa by assets, majority-owned by the Qatar Investment Authority, funded by Qatari and Gulf deposits and lending to the Qatari government and its related entities, with subsidiaries in Turkey and Egypt.
synthesis: The bank is rated A+ on average across all three main agencies, with the last move a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 28 Mar 2024, but one of the three holds a negative outlook while the other two are stable. No capital or liquidity ratios are held here, so there is no peer comparison to make on the figures. The flagged news is that outlook change on 10 Sep 2026, which is the one thing to watch. Qatari state ownership is the main support, and the negative outlook is a signal about the sovereign's position rather than about the bank's own books.
